newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Japanese-funded five billion rupee water supply programme to be launched soon to provide safe drinking water to all by the year 2000, Minister of Public Utilitites Nimal Siripala de Silva says.
Army artillery fire kills seven Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in northeastern Trincomalee district.

Air force unmanned reconnaissance aircraft goes missing over Omanthai in the rebel-cotrolled northern Wanni district. This is the second unmanned aircraft the air force has lost since the beginning of this year.
Government nurses call off plan to strike after government agrees to grant 40 percent of a salary increase requested by nurses. The balance 60 percent increase to be given next year.
Fourteen May Day rallies held by political parties and trade unions in Colombo and in outstations.

United National Party (UNP) will support government proposals to end the ethnic conflict if they don't clash with the UNP's core beliefs, party leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe tells May Day rally.
Air force loses 12th aircraft this year with the disappearance of an unmanned reconnaissance aircraft over rebel-controlled northern Wanni district.
